t22.summary: Augur reports that the Texas Supreme Court has ruled the election law unconstitutional and that Governor Davis, expecting the newly elected legislature and governor to seize the government by force, asks for U.S. troops; Augur declines to act without the President's orders and asks Sheridan whether he is right.

t29.summary: Augur forwards a dispatch from Davis for President Grant warning that unauthorized persons may try to take the state buildings; seven code words are open.

t30.summary: Augur tells Major Russell in Austin that, through Sheridan, the President has no instructions to give, and that he has sent on the Governor's dispatch.

t45.summary: Augur tells Russell that if Davis yields to force without armed collision that is all that can be expected, that neither the President nor the party wants trouble, that he need not recognize either governor, and that Sellers is not to interfere without orders.

system: Word route transposition: cipher words written in rows of 7 or 9, plaintext taken down or up the columns in a route set by an indicator word, with a few arbitraries for names and phrases and filler place names at the end.
